title: Private/VPC: Artifact-stitching & Staged-Fallback Upgrade Contract
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Problem: Customers running Private/VPC installations require a deterministic, low-risk upgrade path when egress is restricted. Existing docs focus on mirrors and offline bootstrap but do not define an artifact-level contract for staged upgrades, signed manifests, or deterministic rollback fences. This ticket defines requirements and acceptance criteria for: (1) artifact-stitching (delta snapshot delivery with signature verification), (2) staged-fallback policies (incremental canary + quorum rollback fences), and (3) operator-sidecar preflight checks for disconnected clusters.
scope: In scope: define network and artifact validation requirements for air-gapped and limited-egress Private/VPC installs; acceptance tests for upgrade choreography using signed manifests and delta snapshots; operator-sidecar preflight and post-upgrade health checks; documented playbook for staged fallback and rollback fences.
Out of scope: building a new mirror CDN service; interactive installer UX redesign; changes to customer KMS integrations beyond signature verification requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Signed manifest specification (v2) published: includes artifact list, per-artifact sha256, incremental delta pointers, and timestamp; acceptance requires design doc and example manifest used in CI.

Artifact-stitching flow validated: Private deploy can apply a delta snapshot chain (base -> delta1 -> delta2) with verification at each step; end-to-end test in an air-gapped testbed demonstrates successful upgrade using only pre-seeded artifacts + signed manifests.

Operator-sidecar preflight implemented: sidecar verifies node-level checksum, available disk/pvc headroom threshold, and expected kernel/container runtimes before applying an upgrade; test simulates degraded node and must block upgrade with clear error code.

Staged-fallback policy enforced: canary cohort defined (configurable % of nodes), automatic quorum health check (latency, error-rate, cpu) with configurable rollback fence thresholds; automated rollback succeeds and restores prior container image + KV-state snapshot within SLO.

Zero-egress verification matrix: documented network egress rules required for each supported upgrade mode (fully air-gapped, mirror-sync, minimal egress for signature CRL checks) and acceptance includes a test that performs upgrade with all non-required egress blocked.

Operator-runbook and playbook published: step-by-step operator actions for manual intervention, including commands to verify signatures, inspect delta chain, and trigger forced rollback; runbook reviewed and signed off by SRE and Support.

CI smoke scenarios: at least 4 automated scenarios run in PRs — (1) full offline install + upgrade, (2) delta-only upgrade, (3) partial network partition during upgrade, (4) rollback after canary failure. All must pass in the private-upgrade pipeline.
Backward-compatible fallback: customers using existing offline mirror workflows must be able to opt into artifact-stitching without breaking prior mirror-based upgrades; migration guide included.
decisions: Prefer signed manifests + per-artifact hashes over ad-hoc tarball checksums to enable partial deltas and fine-grained verification.
Use operator-sidecar as enforcement point rather than modifying core operator to minimize blast radius and simplify rollback semantics.
Canary cohort size will be configurable but default to 2% of total nodes for large clusters; default quorum thresholds conservative to favor availability-first.
Do not introduce a new external mirror service in this scope; rely on customer-managed artifact distribution or existing mirror tooling.
